purpose: Heavy Rebuild v2 clean-master architectural and service program for the authoritative abandoned truck stop asset, preserving a recognizable long-haul roadside service complex with truck circulation, fueling, parking, driver amenities, food service, maintenance support, deliveries, utilities, signage, terrain seating and coherent abandonment damage.
ground_program: highway or arterial approach separates heavy-truck ingress and egress from passenger-vehicle access where practical, with turning geometry that visibly accommodates articulated vehicles rather than treating the site as a generic parking lot
truck forecourt contains fuel lanes, canopy or weather protection where appropriate, pump/service islands and a clear pull-through relationship between road access, fueling and long-haul parking
long-haul parking provides recognizable tractor-trailer bays, circulation aisles and pedestrian routes toward the principal building without forcing drivers through active fueling lanes

principal building provides public entrance, cashier or service counter, convenience retail, driver lounge or waiting space, food-service area and public sanitation as a coherent roadside-service program
driver-support spaces include showers, laundry or equivalent long-haul amenities where footprint permits, separated from food preparation and public retail circulation
back-of-house program includes food and retail storage, refrigeration where required, staff/service space, refuse handling and direct delivery access that does not depend on the public entrance
service or maintenance component, when present, provides vehicle-accessible bays, tool or parts storage and a safe relationship to truck circulation without blocking the fueling forecourt
fuel storage, electrical service, water, drainage, wastewater, grease/refuse and mechanical systems are represented as serviceable infrastructure with plausible protected access
parking aprons, curbs, drainage, sign foundations, utility pads and any retaining features seat the complex into terrain without floating paving, buried doors or disconnected road elevations
upper_program: roof structure supports exhausts, vents, signs and mechanical equipment with plausible curbs, frames or service platforms
canopies over fueling or pedestrian areas use columns, beams or equivalent visible support and do not terminate in unsupported floating roof planes
freestanding truck-stop signage uses a foundation, mast and sign frame appropriate to roadside visibility and wind exposure
any occupied second-floor, motel-like or mezzanine program uses supported architectural stairs, landings and guards rather than equipment ladders
rooftop service equipment retains a credible maintenance route from an interior service point or dedicated external access
circulation: tractor-trailers can enter, fuel, reach parking or service bays and exit without impossible turning paths or routine reversing through customer pedestrian zones
passenger vehicles have a distinct practical route to public parking and the principal entrance
pedestrian circulation connects truck parking and passenger parking to the building while minimizing crossings of active fueling and heavy-vehicle lanes
staff circulation connects cashier, retail, food service, storage, sanitation, deliveries and service exits as a coherent back-of-house network
delivery and refuse routes reach their service areas without passing through customer dining, lounge or retail spaces
maintenance access reaches fuel, electrical, plumbing, wastewater, mechanical, canopy and roof-service infrastructure
equipment-only ladders do not substitute for architectural stairs in occupied spaces
damage_constraints: the abandoned derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a truck stop through surviving heavy-vehicle circulation, fuel-lane, long-haul parking, principal-building and roadside-sign relationships

favor localized canopy failure, pump damage, vehicle impact, storefront loss, kitchen or electrical fire, water intrusion, vandalism, scavenging and vegetation encroachment over uniform random deletion
canopy, sign or roof collapse must follow identifiable structural failure and resolve attached lights, ducts, fascia and supports so floating fragments are not left behind
fuel-system damage may expose pumps, piping or storage infrastructure but must preserve enough of the receiving-storage-dispensing relationship to communicate the former function
building damage should preserve at least one viable exploration route from a public entrance toward the service counter and driver-support spaces
truck lanes, parking aprons, drainage and highway connection should remain spatially coherent after damage rather than becoming disconnected slabs or impassable decorative clutter
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master
